newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Safeway joins scramble for Ireland.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Safeway joins scramble for Ireland.

text.p: British supermarket group Safeway Plc joined the retail rush into Ireland on Thursday through a joint venture that will be operating 19 stores by 1999.
Safeway, one of the leading names in British food retailing, has agreed to form a 50-50 joint venture with Fitzwilton Plc, which operates the Wellworth chain in Northern Ireland.

The joint venture will acquire nine stores and four sites from Fitzwilton for 65 million pounds ($106.6 million) and take a further six stores under licence. The 15 stores have a share of 11 percent of the market in Northern Ireland.
The shops and new sites are all in the British province of Northern Ireland but Safeway is also keen to expand into the Irish Republic, where the economy is growing rapidly.
"We are currently actively seeking sites in the south (Irish Republic)," Safeway finance director Simon Laffin told Reuters.
He said the local knowledge of partners Fitzwilton would be an asset. Leading Irish businessman Tony O'Reilly is the chairman of Fitzwilton and a major shareholder.
Laffin said the venture would aim to open three or four stores annually, "some in the north, but probably more in the south".

Leading British food retailer Tesco agreed in March to pay 630 million pounds to acquire the Irish stores owned by Associated British Foods. That gave Tesco 75 stores in the Irish Republic and 34 in Northern Ireland.
Rival supermarket group Sainsbury Plc plans seven stores in Northern Ireland while a number of other leading British high street retailers have recently opened in Dublin.
Laffin said Safeway had no qualms about expanding into Northern Ireland at a time when the province was once again tense following the IRA murder of two policemen earlier this week.
He noted that Wellworth had built a successful business during almost 30 years of continuing sectarian conflict.
Safeway shares fell 7p to 353p by 1145 GMT on Thursday as leading London stocks dipped lower.
Share analysts said the deal, long rumoured, appeared a neat way into the Irish market.
"The Wellworth stores are not that impressive physically and there is a lot that Safeway should be able to do to drive up sales," said Paul Smiddy of Credit Lyonnais Laing.
The stores will be converted to the Safeway brand and the venture plans to spend 50 million pounds on upgrading them and adding features such as dry cleaning, creches and petrol stations.
It expects to spend a further 40 million pounds on the four new sites it plans to open in the next two years.
Safeway pledged to safeguard the jobs of 2,000 Wellworth staff and said that a further 1,000 jobs should be created in the new stores. ($ = 0.609 British Pounds)
